### **Recursive Definition**

Let $ a(n) $ denote the value at position $ n $. The sequence is defined as follows:

$$
a(n) = 
\begin{cases}
31, & \text{if } n = 0 \\
1, & \text{if } n \equiv 2 \text{ or } 8 \pmod{10} \text{ and } 1 \leq n < 10 \\
7, & \text{if } n = 5 \\
2, & \text{if } 1 \leq n < 10 \text{ and not in the above cases} \\
62, & \text{if } n \geq 10 \text{ and } n \equiv 0 \pmod{10} \\
a(n - 10), & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
$$

---

### **Explanation**

- **Base case:** $ a(0) = 31 $, which is the first element of the sequence.
- **For $ 1 \leq n < 10 $:** The values are determined directly based on $ n \mod 10 $:
  - $ a(n) = 1 $ if $ n \equiv 2 $ or $ 8 \pmod{10} $
  - $ a(5) = 7 $ is a special case
  - All other values in this range are $ 2 $
- **For $ n \geq 10 $:** The sequence becomes periodic with period 10, except for positions that are multiples of 10:
  - If $ n \equiv 0 \pmod{10} $, then $ a(n) = 62 $
  - Otherwise, $ a(n) = a(n - 10) $, which means the value is the same as the one 10 positions earlier
